{{Short description|Concept in abstract algebra}}
In [[group theory]], a discipline within [[abstract algebra]], a '''special group''' is a [[finite group]] of [[prime power]] [[order of a group|order]] that is either [[elementary abelian group|elementary abelian]] itself or of class&nbsp;2 with its [[derived group]], its [[center (group theory)|center]], and its [[Frattini subgroup]] all equal and elementary abelian {{harv|Gorenstein|1980|loc=p.183}}.  A special group of order ''p''<sup>''n''</sup> that has class 2 and whose derived group has order ''p'' is called an [[extra special group]].
